payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed, with no visible opening remaining along its closure?
node.criteria: Pass if the jacket's front panels meet along the entire closure and no opening remains. Fail if any visible opening remains along the closure. Unknown if the closure is obscured or the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether it is fully closed.
node.binding: Assess the same jacket and closure as in s1. Full closure is the requested endpoint; partial closure is not complete fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The same jacket remains visibly open in the edited image: its front panel hangs away from her body, leaving an opening along the closure.

dependencies.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image, with a panel hanging away from her body, rather than brought together compared with the source.

fulfillment: The node’s binding and question are semantically aligned with the requested edit, and the traces are valid, queried, and high-confidence; there is no transport or schema failure to fix. The mismatch is that the evaluator concludes “absent” from evidence that the jacket is still open, while the reference says the aggregate edit is complete. Do not force “yes” from the reference label or weaken the fully-closed criterion. Instead, investigate whether the checks are binding to the same jacket and comparing the correct source and edited regions: the images show a substantial pose change, and the edited jacket’s front is partly obscured by its draped panel, so a visible opening may be difficult to assess. Make the checks distinguish “not visibly closed” from “clearly open,” and preserve unresolved status when occlusion or pose prevents a reliable judgment. Also ensure s1 assesses progress relative to the source rather than treating a changed pose or panel position alone as proof of no progress; the fulfillment node should apply its existing complete/partial/absent rules only to supported check outcomes.

Keep “visible opening” distinct from “not clearly shown to be closed”: when the closure is obscured or the changed view prevents a reliable assessment, return unknown rather than fail. Preserve the full-closure requirement; investigate whether the apparent opening is actually along the closure before treating it as evidence of non-fulfillment."}
